brief: A wall-hung spice rack: at least three bins, hung from keyhole hangers.

requirements.evidence: Three full-depth hex base cells in a row (piece at q=-1,0,1, r=0) form the rack body, joined with joint bolts and capped on all open faces. Check_build is clean (meshClash clear, no issues). I did not verify the wall-facing orientation visually; the look tool did not show the parts.
Three hex-bin-full-div3 bins (3 compartments each) at cells (-1,0), (0,0), (1,0): bin:-1,0,0, bin:0,0,0, bin:1,0,0.

Three hex-acc-keyhole accessories, one per bin cell, on face slot 1: accessory:0#-1,0#1, accessory:0#0,0#1, accessory:0#1,0#1. The configurator accepted them, but I did not confirm slot 1 faces the wall, so the hanging orientation is unverified.

finish.summary: Built a horizontal row of three full hex base cells with a three-compartment bin in each (nine spice compartments total), three keyhole hangers on one face of each cell, caps on open faces and joint bolts locking the row. The configurator reports no issues and a clear mesh check. No spice props were added because none exist in the prop library. The wall-facing direction of the keyhole faces was not verified visually, and nothing was checked for load, material or strength.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
